edges.description: Loss of SWI/SNF antagonism of PRC2 leaves EZH2-driven H3K27 methylation unopposed, creating an oncogenic dependency.
Unopposed PRC2 repression and reduced enhancer occupancy by residual SWI/SNF complexes silence differentiation and tumor-suppressor programs, sustaining an undifferentiated proliferative tumor state.
The proliferative, infiltrative tumor invades local soft tissues and disseminates, with a characteristic propensity for regional lymph node and pulmonary spread.
Proliferative growth of epithelioid and spindle tumor cells produces the clinically apparent soft-tissue or dermal mass.
Superficial distal tumor invasion can break down overlying skin and present as a non-healing ulcer.
Metastatic dissemination from the primary tumor commonly involves regional lymph nodes.
Hematogenous dissemination of invasive epithelioid sarcoma cells frequently seeds the lungs, the second leading site of initial metastasis after regional lymph nodes.
Complete absence of nuclear INI1 (BAF47) immunostaining directly reflects loss of SMARCB1 protein expression in epithelioid sarcoma tumor cells.

nodes.description: Loss of SMARCB1 reduces mSWI/SNF affinity and occupancy at tissue-specific enhancers and bivalent promoters while unopposed PRC2 represses differentiation and tumor-suppressor genes, driving sustained tumor cell proliferation in a poorly differentiated epithelial-mesenchymal hybrid state and producing locally expansile soft-tissue tumor nodules.

evidence.reference_title: Translational Aspects of Epithelioid Sarcoma: Current Consensus.
evidence.snippet: In the context of MRT, the loss of SMARCB1 lowers the affinities of mSWI/SNF complexes for chromatin, significantly reducing the occupancy of aberrant mSWI/SNF complexes on enhancers and bivalent gene promoters; these changes lead to the repression of key genes involved in cell differentiation and tumor suppression( 14 ).

nodes.description: SWI/SNF normally opposes Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) at enhancers and bivalent promoters. When SMARCB1 is lost, PRC2/EZH2 catalytic activity is unopposed, increasing trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me3) and epigenetically repressing differentiation and tumor-suppressor genes. SMARCB1-deficient tumors acquire a synthetic-lethal dependency on EZH2 activity, forming the mechanistic basis for therapeutic EZH2 inhibition.

evidence.snippet: INI1 (hSNF5/SMARCB1), a member of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex located on chromosome 22q11.2, is deleted or/or mutated in strictly defined malignant rhabdoid tumors (MRT) of infancy. Recent studies suggest that some epithelioid sarcomas (ES) also show inactivation of INI1.

evidence.snippet: In total, 127 of 136 (93%) ES cases showed complete absence of INI1 expression, including 58 (91%) conventional ES, 61 (95%) proximal-type ES, and all 8 (100%) hybrid ES.

evidence.snippet: Most EpS harbor homozygous deletions, while in a smaller subset only heterozygous SMARCB1 loss-of-function (LOF) alterations are detected( 7 , 8 , 15 , 16 ).

nodes.description: Biallelic somatic inactivation of SMARCB1 (INI1/BAF47/SNF5), most commonly via homozygous 22q11.2 deletions, disables a core subunit of the canonical BAF (cBAF) and polybromo-associated BAF (PBAF) SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complexes. This is the defining molecular event in over 90% of both classic and proximal-type epithelioid sarcomas and produces the diagnostic loss of nuclear INI1 immunostaining.

evidence.reference_title: Translational Aspects of Epithelioid Sarcoma: Current Consensus.
evidence.snippet: SMARCB1 biallelic inactivation drives the pathogenesis of virtually all EpS. SMARCB1 encodes a subunit of two of the three SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complexes (canonical BAF (cBAF), polybromo-associated BAF (PBAF), but not non-canonical BAF (ncBAF)), which regulates gene transcription through nucleosomes modifications( 14 ).
